background: BNP Paribas is the largest bank in the eurozone, a universal bank with retail networks in France, Belgium, Italy and Luxembourg, a large corporate and investment bank, and consumer finance, leasing and asset management arms.
synthesis: All three main agencies rate the bank at A+ on average, all on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. On the reported ratios it sits at the weak end of EU and Nordic banks, with CET1 of 13.0%, leverage of 4.4%, LCR of 135% and NSFR of 109% all in the bottom quarter. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods, so the gap is structural rather than a recent slide, and the ratings look past it to the scale and diversity of the group. The flagged news, the newest on 5 Oct 2026, is all positive, on earnings and a strong rise in profit.
